7.text: OpenAI completed an $11B funding tranche at a $1.25T valuation, with SoftBank and MGX in talks, and launched a cybersecurity model plus a Hacktron partnership. Anthropic's ~$70B IPO filing was retracted, it paid AP for content, and its lofty valuation faces investor pushback affecting Microsoft.

16.text: Microsoft appears only incidentally as a top holding in the tech-heavy ETFs (VUG, MGK, QQQ, VGT, FTEC, IYW), so the articles report no Microsoft-specific news; their focus is ETF performance, fees, concentration and AI sell-off risk.

6.text: Market-research reports project growth in digital transformation, next-gen computing, virtual machines, and clinical genomics software, naming Microsoft among key vendors. Concentrix and Postman launched offerings in the Microsoft Marketplace, while other articles mention Microsoft only as a listed competitor.

14.text: Microsoft beat Q1 FY2027 estimates with 18.8% revenue growth and 48% Azure growth, sending shares up over 6% as analysts raised targets to as high as $722. Coverage debated valuation, capex, and free cash flow, with some downgrades citing limited upside after a 74% five-year run.

5.text: AI debt has hit record levels as chip stocks sold off sharply and investors questioned whether the massive infrastructure spending boom is sustainable. Analysts warn neocloud players like CoreWeave and Oracle face rising credit risk, while Bernie Sanders said Big Tech won't be bailed out; Microsoft is mentioned only as barely moving amid the split.

9.text: Microsoft declined to renew data center capacity contracts with Nscale in Texas and is winding down an Oracle AI infrastructure deal, consolidating its neocloud partnerships and prioritizing its own data centers. It is also pressing the Trump administration to block an expected ban on Chinese data center technology.

12.text: Microsoft is tightening oversight of data-center projects run by IREN, Nebius, and Nscale, reportedly delaying its Q3 2026 buildout by about $5 billion and pushing IREN's Texas site back weeks or months. IREN's AI cloud revenue nearly tripled to $200 million, with its $4 billion ARR target slipping to January at Microsoft's request.

19.text: AWS grew 39% to $46B but trails Azure’s 48% and Google Cloud’s 103%. Microsoft and Amazon gained $400B in market value as data-center constraints could boost cloud pricing power; both shrugged off Ohio data-center bans.

17.text: Alphabet shares fell sharply over the week, with articles citing AI infrastructure spending, cloud growth, and valuation as buy signals. Microsoft is barely mentioned; the story bears on it only as a hyperscaler comparison.

18.text: Tesla, SpaceX, Amazon, Netflix, Lam Research, SoFi, Apple, Meta, Home Depot, and Boeing joined 56+ companies refusing to let their shares trade on the planned OKX-ICE tokenized venue, meaning all Magnificent Seven stocks have opted out. Separately, dYdX's Arcus opened stock-token collateral to all perps traders with a $20,000 cap. Microsoft isn't named among objectors.

20.text: Palantir beat Q3 estimates with 96% revenue growth to $2.3 billion and raised guidance; Arista Networks beat earnings, guided 2027 revenue to about $18.5 billion, and its stock rose 6%. Neither article mentions Microsoft, though both reflect surging AI-related demand.
